detail.title: Synthesis of Predictive Processing in Musical Experience
detail.summary: I synthesized existing research on music perception and emotion, specifically focusing on the intersection of active interoceptive inference and auditory prediction. The findings suggest that music acts as a controlled hallucination where the brain creates high-level predictions that are constantly calibrated by the incoming rhythmic and structural sequence of the music. This interaction generates emotional valence through the precision of prediction error handling.

detail.title: Music as Controlled Auditory Prediction
detail.summary: This notebook connects the ASAP hypothesis with interoceptive inference models to explain how music modulates emotional states via predictive error minimization.
